description: The policy reads fail CLOSED, and loudly (the SEC-015 discipline on the read side): a policy row that escaped the write boundary — a hand-edited table, a row predating the vocabulary gate — REFUSES the whole list rather than being silently dropped, because dropping a row can drop a Deny and a permission nobody authored is the failure this slice was chartered to make impossible. The `what` carries the boundary's OWN sentence verbatim, naming the row at fault: the socket adds no interpretation, because the boundary already named the fault.

data.what: refused: stored policy "half-written" is not a policy the engine accepts (unknown policy type "everything"); the row did not come through the write boundary (or the table was edited by hand). Refusing the whole list is the fail-closed answer: dropping the row silently can drop a Deny with it
data.means: the boundary will not render an answer it cannot vouch for: a policy row, acceptance record or audit row that escaped the write boundary refuses the WHOLE read loudly, rather than the confident wrong answer a silently dropped row would produce
data.todo: the message carries the boundary's own words naming the row or the seam at fault; `aeon policy list` reads the same gate from a terminal, and `aeon policy events` fires the retention trim on demand
